rationale: Evidence: iteration 6 (score 929.4, the best so far) finishes all 60 development trials. Per track, oval finished 20/20 at 2.36 s, s-bend 20/20 at 2.45 s, and slalom 20/20 at 2.66 s (previously 0/20 to 1/20). The slalom max_error is 0.0215 against an off-track limit of 0.06 m, so there is real margin. The score is now close to its ceiling for this geometry: about 500 for completion, 250 for progress, roughly 105 from line loss (1 event), roughly 65 from rms_error (about 0.01), and about 12 from time (2.4 s). The remaining levers are small: time (each 0.1 s is about 2 points), and line-loss events (one per run, worth up to about 15 points). Lighter mass and shorter body fixed the slalom but made the oval slower (2.10 s to 2.36 s), so the speed setting is the cheapest lever to recover time. Change: base_speed 1.0 to 1.1, a 10% increase. The slalom has about 0.04 m of margin and the oval and s-bend have time budget, so this should cut roughly 0.1 to 0.15 s per track, worth about 2 to 3 points. Everything else is unchanged (geometry, kp 4.5, ki 0.02, kd 1.0, sensor layout, line_loss) so the effect of speed is isolated. Expected result: score about 930 to 935 with all tracks still finishing, and slalom max_error still well below 0.06. Risk: higher speed may push slalom max_error up; if slalom finishes fall below 20/20, revert to 1.0. Hypotheses: (1) the single line-loss event per run probably occurs at the start or the finish when the sensors leave the tape, so it may not be fixable with gains; (2) if oscillation stays low, kd could drop slightly to reduce lag; (3) rms_error on the s-bend (0.016) is the main remaining tracking term. Measurements requested: completion, completion_time and progress to confirm the speed gain, line_loss_events to see when the loss occurs, and max_error and steering_oscillation to check slalom margin.
